evidence: Receiving P(48h)=2.98 g/L vs source P(48h)=3.02, 3.06, 2.98 g/L
Receiving DO2(52h)=10.5 mg/L, comparable to sources (10.5-11.5); minimum DO constraint is 2.0 mg/L
Receiving P(12h)=0.047 and P(24h)=0.014 g/L consistent with source lag phase
Source trajectory: P rises to ~8.1-8.4 g/L at 72 h then declines to ~6.4-7.0 at 96 h; receiving shows no deviation suggesting divergence
submission.rationale: At decision time 52 h, the receiving fermentation matches the source batches closely on every comparable measurement: product assays P(12h)=0.047, P(24h)=0.014, P(36h)=1.017, P(48h)=2.984 g/L versus source values ~0.02-0.03, ~0.0-0.02, ~1.02-1.12, and ~2.98-3.06 g/L respectively; and the receiving DO2 trajectory (10.5 mg/L at 52 h, never below ~7.7 mg/L during the observed window) tracks the source pattern with a healthy oxygen margin far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Product is on the source-like growth trajectory (sources reached ~8 g/L by 72 h then declined after ~84-96 h), and no oxygen-constraint violation or receiving-vs-source deviation is evident. Feed reduction would sacrifice the product mass accumulation rate with no DO2 need; increasing air has no benefit given ample DO2 and risks uncharacterized receiving-process behavior. The normal case here needs no intervention.
submission.uncertainty: The receiving process differs from the source (hidden parameters/states unknown), so future divergence after 52 h cannot be ruled out — however the near-exact tracking across 12-48 h assays and DO2 trends gives high confidence in KEEP. The latest product assay is 4 h old (48 h sample), so current true concentration is unobserved; an extra assay could confirm but would not plausibly change the decision given consistent multi-batch agreement. A stop would yield zero counted production and is clearly dominated.

evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52h = 10.49 mg/L, well above the 2 mg/L limit; minimum observed DO2 = 7.77 mg/L at 27.8h
Receiving P assays: 0.047 g/L (12h), 0.014 (24h), 1.017 (36h), 2.984 g/L (48h) — matches source batches' normal production curve (source P at 48h: 3.06, 3.02, 2.98)
Receiving DO2 profile including ~24h dip, 28h jump, and 75h-style recovery mirrors source-1/2/3 trajectories
Forward model KEEP: 576 kg product, min DO 7.20 mg/L, zero oxygen deficit, all 5 sensitivity members feasible
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation is tracking the healthy source-batch trajectories closely: DO2 profile (dip to ~7.8–8.4 mg/L at 24–28h, recovery jumps at 28h) matches all three source batches, and delayed P assays (36h: 1.02 g/L, 48h: 2.98 g/L) match source values (1.02–1.12, 2.98–3.06 g/L). DO2 at 52h is ~10.5 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L minimum with no oxygen deficit. The forward model under KEEP predicts ~576 kg product mass, min DO ~7.2 mg/L, zero below-limit hours, and feasibility across all sensitivity members. Interventions (feed reduction) would lower growth/product formation without any oxygen-constraint benefit; stop would forfeit all production. This is a normal case requiring no intervention.
submission.uncertainty: Forward model is a nominal source-calibrated prediction, not the hidden receiving realization; DO2 is noisy online sensor data with a systematic step at 28h/75h. However, deviation from source baselines is small and consistent across both DO2 and P assays, so KEEP risk is low. If hidden receiving parameters are worse than nominal, min DO margin (7.2 vs 2.0 mg/L limit) is still wide.
